This case is registered as ACP, Yeshwanthapura Sub-Division, Bengaluru has submitted Charge- sheet against the accused persons for the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 355 of IPC,
section 4 of DP Act and Section 3(1)(r), (s) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes(Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text:
2. The brief facts of the prosecution case is that the complainant had made complaint before the Investigating Officer in writing that she married Anand on 23.3.2018, they both lived in the house of the parents of Anand, when she was pregnant, her mother-in-law/accused No.1 and father-in-law/
accused No.2 and sister in law harassed her as the victim was belonging to schedule caste, they even demanded to bring dowry as she was not able to bring the dowry, they did not provided food and did not allowed her to cook or even use the toilet and later they threw her on the streets.

Accordingly,
her husband having 2 brothers and one sister, they are staying in the matrimonial, house.
The mother-in- law though provided accomidation at first, but did not provided house to her husband after marriage, as victim is not belonging to their caste.
As such as she was driven away from the matrimonial house, she made complaint before the jurisdictional police.
3. During the course of investigation the accused were apprehended and produced before this Court and subsequently got enlarged on bail.
After filing of charge sheet, this court took the cognizance of the offences in the charge sheet.

The Charge sheet copy was furnished to the accused persons as contemplated under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
4.
Heard before the charge.

As there was sufficient materials available, charge was framed for the above said offences, read over and explained the accused to the accused persons in vernacular language and they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
5. At trial, the prosecution got examined PW-1 and 2 and placed Ex.P.1 to 7 and closed their side.
In the absence of evidence of material eye witnesses though caste of the victim and accused are not disputed.
The materials placed by the prosecution being insufficient and prosecution side evidence is foreclosed.
No incriminating circumstances appeared against accused persons.
Hence, the recording of statement as required under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed.

6. Heard arguments and perused the documents and other materials available on record.
7.

1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on 17.1.2018 at T.Dasarahalli,
Ravindra Nagar, 19th cross, Muthumariyamma temple, the CWs.1 and 2 got married, later, on 23.3.2018 got register marriage in the Sub-Registrar office, and later were staying in No.224, 17 th cross, Ravindra Nagar, Mallasandra, T.Dasarahalli, within the limits of Bagalgunte police station,
after few months, accused persons being the in-laws of the C.W.1 subjected her to mental and physical cruelty by demanding dowry and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 498(A) of IPC?
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on above said date, time and place the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention have demanded CW1 to bring dowry and thereby committed the offence punishable u/sec.4 of DP Act?
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the aforesaid date, time and place, accused No.3 assaulted C.W.1 with chappal and thereby dishonoured C.W.1 and caused grave and sudden provocation and thereby accused No.3 has committed offence punishable u/s 355 of IPC?
4.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the aforesaid date, time and place, accused persons in furtherance of their common intention accused persons not being the members of SC/ST intentionally insulted/ intimidated as C.W.1 with intent to humiliate the C.W.1 who belongs to schedule caste (Adi Dravida community) in a place within the public view and thereby accused have committed offences punishable u/s 3(1)(r) of SC/ST (POA) Act?

5. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on the aforesaid date, time and place, accused persons in furtherance of their common intention accused persons not being the members of SC/ST have abused C.W.1 who belongs to schedule caste by taking the name of her caste in a place within the public view and thereby accused have committed offences punishable u/s 3(1)(s) of SC/ST (POA) Act?
6. What order?
The prosecution in proof of offence punishable u/s.498A of IPC basically relies on the evidence of complainant and her husband namely son of the accused Nos.1 and 2 and brother of accused No.3.

11. In the case on hand, on considering the entire materials on record, the offence punishable u/s.498A of IPC is statutorily not compoundable offence.

However in the case on hand, the accused persons namely the property standing in the name of accused No.1 has been decided to be given one portion to C.W.2/P.W.2/Anand husband of the victim/ complainant.
As such they have made their own family arrangements.

12. On basis of the settlement between the parties in their family itself, the complainant and C.W.2 both have deposed before this court that they are desiring to compound the alleged offence punishable u/s.498A of IPC.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where the Hon'ble Apex Court was quashed the criminal proceedings having regard to the fact that the dispute between the offender and the victim has been settled all though offences are not compoundable.

It does so as in its opinion, the continuation of criminal proceedings will be of exercises in fatality and justice in the case demands that disputes between the parties is public to end and peace is restored.
Securing the ends of justice being the ultimate guiding factor.

No duty crimes are accepts, which have harmful affect on the public and consist in wrong doing that seriously endangers and threaten the well being of the society and its not safe to leave crime does only because he and the victim have settled the dispute amicably or that victim has been ordered compensation, yet certain crimes have been made compoundable in law, who with or if the compromise of the Court.

(Part 61 and 58)"

sentences.text: The complainant has deposed in chief examination about the facts.
Therefore this court can pass suitable orders considering the materials on record.
15. In the case on hand, in proof of the offence punishable u/s.4 of DP Act, the Investigating Officer has specifically recorded further statement of the complainant as per Ex.P.4 on 20.6.2019.
The complainant has specifically denied about giving her statement further on 31.5.2019 and 20.6.2019 as per Ex.P.3 and 4.
Only in the further statement the demand of dowry has been specified, in the complaint Ex.P.1
the demand of the dowry made by the accused persons has not been specified but only as the victim was thrown on the streets from the matrimonial house she was forced to lodge complaint.
As when the property has been made available to C.W.2 husband of complainant, the desire to compound deserves to have some consideration so as to compound the alleged offence.
Therefore in the case on hand, to consider the ingredients of alleged offence punishable u/s.4 of DP.Act there are no other materials placed by the prosecution, apart from hostility of complainant.
16. The complainant has deposed that accused No.3 has assaulted C.W.1 with chappal, but there are no substantial, corroborative evidence to prove the alleged offence.
The complainant has compromised with the accused persons and does not support case of prosecution.

17. The arguments of learned counsel for the accused that accused and victim may be permitted as there is child birth to the victim and C.W.2, parties have agreed to compromise is reasonable which can be considered as per the provisions of law.

Therefore in the absence of documents and materials as per the prosecution, charge sheet being missing on certain charge in the narration of the complainant, being the material witness who does not support the same this court is satisfied to answer Point No.1 to 3 in the Negative.
18. POINT NOS.4 AND 5:

In the case on hand, to prove the ingredients of the alleged offence punishable under Sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of SC/ST (POA) Amendment Act, 2014, accused have done any overt act so as to cause ingredients of offence under Sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of SC/ST (POA) Amendment Act in the public is not forthcoming from either in complaint or from the materials placed on record.
The witness namely, CW-2 is husband of C.W.1.

Under these circumstances, in the absence of any independent public witnesses being made in the charge sheet and as per the complainant narration of the complaint discloses it is the apprehension of the complainant that accused may abandon the complainant as he is avoiding to take back the complainant she was forced to lodge complaint.
Lastly, accused persons abused the complainant cannot be considered in the public view or in a public place.

19. In fact, the accused persons having abused the complainant in filthy language and also by taking her caste, the IO has not collected all the records or other particulars, which are direct evidence so as to consider the offence being committed by accused persons.

Under these circumstances, in the absence of materials placed by the prosecution, this court is obliged to answer point Nos.4 and 5 for consideration taken up simultaneously and are answered in the negative.
